iptables -I INPUT 1 -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

2) OpenVPN (UDP port 1194)

3) WireGuard (UDP port 51820)

4) IPsec (IKE and NAT-T: UDP ports 500 and 4500)

candidate_response:
Short answer: UDP 1194 is the default port/protocol only for OpenVPN (community/OpenVPN Server) — it is not the universal or “official” VPN port for every product. I can confirm precisely for your production environment, but I need to know which VPN product/version you run (OpenVPN, WireGuard, Cisco AnyConnect/ASA, strongSwan/Libreswan/IKEv2, Palo Alto GlobalProtect, SSTP, etc.).

Common VPN products and their usual ports/protocols (defaults — all are configurable):
- OpenVPN (community/OpenVPN Server): UDP 1194 (default). Can be run on TCP (often TCP 443) if configured that way.
- WireGuard: UDP 51820 (default ListenPort; configurable).
- IPsec / IKEv2 (site-to-site and many clients): UDP 500 (IKE/ISAKMP) and UDP 4500 (NAT‑T). Also requires IP protocol ESP (IP proto 50) for non‑NAT flows.
- L2TP over IPsec: UDP 500, UDP 4500 and UDP 1701 (plus ESP where applicable).
- SSTP (Microsoft): TCP 443.
- SSL/TLS-based appliances (AnyConnect-like): TCP 443 for TLS control; many implementations use DTLS (UDP) for the data channel (often on the same port) and will fall back to TCP 443 if UDP is blocked.
- PPTP (legacy): TCP 1723 plus GRE (IP proto 47).

So: if your VPN server is OpenVPN with default configuration, then yes, UDP 1194 is the port you should open. If you run a different product, open the product-specific ports listed above instead.

- On Linux: sudo ss -lntu or sudo ss -tulnp to list listeners and their protocols/ports; then search for the relevant port or service name. For OpenVPN specifically, check the server config (e.g., sudo grep -E '^(proto|port)' /etc/openvpn/*.conf).

- Prefer phishing‑resistant factors (FIDO2/security keys or platform authenticators) for password reset/recovery where feasible.

TOTP (authenticator app) will only be enforced for password resets if the reset flow or policy explicitly requires TOTP (or requires a registered software‑token); otherwise the reset flow will accept whichever MFA methods are enabled/allowed (SMS, phone call, push, hardware keys/WebAuthn, backup codes, etc.).

1. Identify the IdP/product handling authentication (Azure AD / Microsoft Entra, Okta, Auth0, AWS Cognito, Keycloak, a custom system, etc.).
2. In the IdP admin console, open the password‑reset / self‑service password reset (SSPR) or authentication/flows/policies area and look for which authentication methods are allowed and whether a specific method (e.g., Authenticator app / TOTP) is required for resets.

- Auth0: Dashboard > Security > Multi‑factor Auth and the hosted pages/flow settings; review logs for used factors.
